decisions.location: Current Abstract: described prior manual-food bias; independently verified2016and2021original findings
decisions.quote: A previous study with Virtual Reality (VR) and online motion-capture quantified this approach bias towards food and non-food cues in a controlled VR environment with hand movements. The aim of this study was to test the specificity of a manual approach bias for high-calorie food in grasp movements compared to low-calorie food and neutral objects of different complexity, namely, simple balls and geometrically more complex office tools.
decisions.reason: Both complete original reports are available:2016grasp/ward food-versus-ball findings include faster food collection, whereas2021adds office-tool complexity controls and reports a slower food collection contrast with faster earlier movement stages. The current abstract describes an earlier VR/manual approach-bias study broadly, uses office controls and finds faster high-calorie grasp/collection, but its full body/in-text attribution remains unavailable. Task resemblance does not alone exclude a later follow-up from the closest chain or establish whether both reported findings are retested. Thus allocation relative to existing1827remains an actual current-body/finding-attribution limit after original-source attempts. No second original from DOI/year alone. The latest expert p<.001claim for Max onset is not adopted: the verified original context distinguishes onset/contact tests and collection. All raw reasons remain unchanged.

decisions.quote: A previous study with Virtual Reality (VR) and online motion-capture quantified this approach bias towards food and non-food cues in a controlled VR environment with hand movements. The aim of this study was to test the specificity of a manual approach bias for high-calorie food in grasp movements compared to low-calorie food and neutral objects of different complexity, namely, simple balls and geometrically more complex office tools.
decisions.reason: The 2024 source supplies only the abstract (N = 27 healthy participants performing VR grasp/collection and push/warding movements with high-calorie food, low-calorie food, balls, and office tools) and deposited reference list (bib1-bib73), without the full text or in-text citations. Complete primary texts were inspected for the two candidate VR hand-movement food-bias studies in the bibliography: (1) bib60, Schroeder, Lohmann, Butz, & Plewnia (2016, 10.1089/cyber.2015.0311, shipped row 1827; complete accepted manuscript in 19_lohmann_thesis.unrepaired.txt Appendix A), which tested 23 recruited/20 analyzed healthy participants in a VR + Leap Motion grasp/ward task with high-calorie food and balls, finding faster movement onset (p = .05), contact (p = .05), and grasp collection for food than balls (t(19) = 3.692, p = .002) while noting object complexity as an open limitation; and (2) bib39, Max, Schroeder, Blechert, Giel, Ehlis, & Plewnia (2021, 10.1007/s00429-021-02232-9; 02_max_fulltext.all_text.unrepaired.txt), an explicit follow-up (33 recruited/30 analyzed) using VR + Leap Motion (with fNIRS) and touchscreen category selection with food, balls, and office tools, finding faster food movement onset (p = .043) and touch (p = .017) but slower VR food collection (p < .001) in explicit contrast to Schroeder et al. (2016). Although the 2024 grasp/ward task and faster collection finding align more closely with Schroeder et al. (2016), task differences alone do not exclude Max et al. (2021) from the retested chain, and without the 2024 body's in-text citations, unique attribution to row 1827 cannot be conclusively established. Prior adjudication 44eadc8d...json exists; prior state f17d6adb...json does not.

previous_decisions.reason: 1. Unresolved question: The supplied primary source file (texts/a23c52a8487df33f.txt) consists solely of the title, author line, and abstract of Schroeder, Collantoni, Lohmann, Butz, & Plewnia (2024), without the full text or reference list. The abstract states that 'A previous study with Virtual Reality (VR) and online motion-capture quantified this approach bias towards food and non-food cues in a controlled VR environment with hand movements' and retests/extends that manual food approach bias in VR, but never prints the authors, year, title, or DOI of that previous study. 2. Comparison with shipped row: The sole shipped row (input_row_index 1827, 10.1089/cyber.2015.0311) is Schroeder, Lohmann, Butz, & Plewnia (2016), 'Behavioral Bias for Food Reflected in Hand Movements: A Preliminary Study with Healthy Subjects' (Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking, 19(2), 120-126), authored by four of the five authors of the 2024 paper on the same topic. While target_index 0 (the sole blind target, which has empty identity fields) almost certainly corresponds to shipped row 1827, the absence of full text and explicit bibliographic citation in the supplied source text prevents positive primary-source verification of the exact citation identity and absence/equivalence, requiring an undeterminable verdict per the review instructions. 3. Prior adjudication: Neither prior_adjudication_path nor prior_state_path exists for this work.
